headline: AI Elite Lose $18 Billion as Chip Stock Rout Spreads to Asia
author: Cindy Wang and Pui Gwen Yeung

paragraphs.text: Cindy Wang and Pui Gwen Yeung
Thu, November 5, 2026 at 11:22 PM PST 2 min read
(Bloomberg) -- SoftBank Group Corp. founder Masayoshi Son and other tycoons across Asia saw billions erased from their fortunes as a global tech selloff rippled through their companies on Friday.

Twenty-two billionaires from China, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea who rank in the world's 500 richest lost more than $21 billion in combined wealth as of 10 a.m. Hong Kong time, before paring that to more than $18 billion, according to calculations from the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. Son was the biggest loser, with his fortune declining by $3.9 billion to about $29 billion.

Among the hardest hit were the firms at the heart of the AI boom. Those who lost $1 billion or more include Takemitsu Takizaki of electronic sensor maker Keyence Corp., and Singapore's richest person Jason Chang of ASE Technology Holding Co., which assembles and packages semiconductors.
Samsung Electronics Co. shareholders Jay Y. Lee, his mother and sister - one of Asia's richest families - collectively lost about $2.5 billion from their fortunes.

The turmoil also last month hit hedge funds including Tiger Global Management and Whale Rock Capital Management, as concerns over AI investments roiled markets. In Asia, wealthy clients of brokers from Taiwan to Hong Kong faced margin calls on leveraged bets, people familiar with the matter said.

Expectations that a Democrat-controlled House of Representatives and Senate will work to slow construction of data centers — a critical component of AI infrastructure — helped drive technology stocks lower across Asia Friday, following a record $2.3 trillion wipeout in market value of the Nasdaq 100 index. The losses extended a wealth reversal that saw Nvidia Corp.'s Jensen Huang drop out of the world's top ten richest.
